cards.text: Zechariah is a prophet of the LORD (Zechariah 1:1). Right before this, God promised to bring His people back home (Zechariah 10:10). Now the message takes a hard turn: Lebanon is told to open its doors so fire can consume its cedars.

cards.question: With Lebanon's great cedar fallen, the cypress is told to ___.

cards.text: The majestic trees are ruined. That's like hearing the biggest guy at work just got let go, and suddenly EVERYBODY in the office is polishing their résumé.

cards.question: Only the cedars of Lebanon get hit. The rest of the forest is left standing.

cards.text: Then Zechariah says to listen to the wailing of the shepherds, because their glory is in ruins. And they're not the only ones making noise.

cards.question: While the shepherds wail, the young lions are roaring. Why are the young lions roaring?

answers.text: The thickets of the Jordan are destroyed
The shepherds are chasing them off
They have cornered a flock of sheep

cards.text: Then the prophet passes along what the LORD his God says. God has a shepherding job for him, and it's a heavy one.

cards.question: God tells the prophet to pasture a flock. What kind of flock is it?

answers.text: A flock lost in the hills

cards.text: And it's grim. The people who buy these sheep slaughter them without remorse.

cards.question: Then there are the people who sell the sheep. What do the sellers say?

answers.text: They bless the LORD because they are rich
They weep over the flock they lost
They swear they will never sell again

cards.question: At least the flock's own shepherds have compassion on them.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He will no longer have compassion on the people of the land. And He isn't done speaking.

cards.question: The LORD says each man in the land will fall into someone's hands. Whose hands?

cards.text: So the prophet takes the job and picks up two staffs, one named Favor and one named Union. Naming your tools? Friend, I named every station in my bakery, so no judgment here.

cards.question: Out of the whole flock marked for slaughter, the prophet pastures the ___ ones especially.

cards.text: In one month, the prophet dismisses three shepherds. THREE shepherds in ONE month? Friend, that's not a team, that's a revolving door.

cards.question: The prophet and the flock get along just fine.
The prophet has grown impatient with the flock, and the flock detests him. What does he do?

answers.text: He asks God for a new flock
He sells them at the market

cards.text: He tells them, 'Let the dying die, and the perishing perish.' Friend, that is NOT a two-weeks' notice.
Next, the prophet takes the staff called Favor and cuts it in two. Snap.

cards.question: Cutting the staff called Favor revokes something. What does it revoke?

answers.text: The covenant with all the nations
The promise of rain for the land
The deal with the sheep traders

cards.text: It's revoked on that very day. And some of the flock are watching him.

cards.question: The afflicted of the flock who watch the staff called Favor get cut know it was the word of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the prophet brings up his wages. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for years and never got paid a single cent, so I'm leaning in on this one.

cards.question: The prophet tells them they have to pay his wages, no matter what they think.
They weigh out the prophet's wages: thirty pieces of silver. Then the LORD tells him to throw it to someone. Who?

cards.text: Then comes this line about the silver: 'this magnificent price at which they valued me.' I think somebody's saying 'magnificent' with one eyebrow WAY up.

cards.question: The prophet throws the thirty pieces of silver to the potter out in the marketplace.

cards.text: Then the prophet takes his second staff, the one called Union, and cuts that one in two as well.

cards.question: Cutting the staff called Union breaks something. What does it break?

answers.text: The brotherhood between Judah and Israel
The covenant with all the nations
The alliance between Israel and Egypt

cards.text: Then the LORD tells the prophet to take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd. Now THAT is a costume change I did not see coming.

cards.question: The LORD says He will raise up a shepherd in the land who will heal the broken and seek the young.
Instead of caring for the flock, the shepherd the LORD raises up ___ the choice sheep.

cards.text: The LORD's message ends with a woe on the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock. Friend, I spent years stuck in a junk drawer where walking out was never even an option, and this guy HAS the option and walks anyway.

cards.question: The LORD's woe on the worthless shepherd includes a sword. Where does the LORD say it should strike him?

answers.text: His arm and his right eye

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'May his arm be completely withered and his right eye utterly blinded!' Heavy words to end on, friend.

findings.problem: Cards 12-13 cover the lack of compassion and falling into the hands of a neighbor and king, but omit the rest of verse 6: those hands will devastate the land, and the LORD will not deliver it. These concluding judgments are not covered anywhere else.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The earlier cards give no basis for choosing 'afflicted' rather than 'youngest,' since either could plausibly describe sheep needing special care. The baker therefore has to guess an unseen word from verse 7 rather than reason out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The walkthrough stops verse 9 after the dying die and the perishing perish. It never covers the verse's concluding judgment that those who remain will devour one another's flesh.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This stop becomes a guessing game. Cards 2, 6, 7, 9 and 16, five of its nine choice cards, give no prior basis for reasoning out the covenant, the optional wages, the potter, the location, or the sword's target. That is more than a few discovery questions within the stop.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Marking the marketplace statement false only tells the baker where the silver was not thrown. No card states verse 13's actual location: the prophet threw the silver to the potter in the house of the LORD.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The covenant with all the nations' describes something that actually happens in this passage: verse 10 says cutting the staff called Favor revoked that covenant. It is therefore not false everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
